confidence_notes: Restaurant, coffee and beer anchors are based on searches of aggregated cost-of-living indexes (Numbeo Jan 2026, world-prices.com 2026, whereandwhen.net). These show an inexpensive meal at about KES 250-300, a mid-range meal for two at about KES 3,000, a cappuccino at about KES 285-430 and a domestic beer at about KES 250-280. I converted at roughly KES 129 per USD and raised the figures slightly, because these indexes are crowd-sourced and visitors in tourist areas like Nyali and the beach strip usually pay more than residents. I could not find a city-wide average for cocktails or wine. Those two anchors come from venue price ranges in travel and nightlife guides (Nyali rooftop and tapas bars at about KES 600-1,200 per cocktail and KES 500-900 per glass of wine; a local bar at about KES 400-700 per cocktail), plus one 2026 index average of about $4.80 for a cocktail. I also checked them against the usual local ratio to beer. Upscale hotel bars charge far more (KES 1,000-2,000), so I left them out of the typical price. These two anchors are less reliable than the food anchors. Accommodation anchors are model estimates from general knowledge only, without any search or live listings. Mombasa has few registered hostels, so the dorm and private-room estimates are the least certain. Three-star prices vary by season and by location (beach or town). The FX date and rate were reported in a web search summary that cited the RBA exchange-rates page; I did not read the RBA page directly.
comparable_city_reasoning: Mombasa is a coastal tourist city in East Africa where local prices are low but tourist-zone prices are higher. I compared it with Zanzibar/Stone Town, Dar es Salaam and Nairobi, using a coastal-resort premium for drinks and tourist-area dining.
